props.title: Adding the DJ to a band booking.
props.lede: Once we’re in the building the evening is already committed, so adding the DJ to a band booking costs far less than hiring one separately. The band’s last set ends, the DJ picks up through the same sound system, and the music carries straight on.

props.html: A duo through cocktails and dinner with the DJ carrying the rest of the night is a common Denver holiday party booking, and the handoff is planned with your run of show. Booked on their own, a Denver DJ carrying a night with production lighting runs $2,500 to $6,000 in this market.
This figure comes from published 2026 market guides, read September 2026. Signet provides prices for a specific date on request.

rows.text: The most common single booking of the corporate season, from a downtown Denver hotel ballroom to an office floor.
Launches, closing dinners that turn into parties, and member events with a late finish, on one contract with the paperwork your office needs.
A milestone birthday or an anniversary that ends with everybody dancing, and the Halloween party, the one night a house books a DJ before anything else.
A common wedding booking is live musicians for the ceremony and the cocktail hour, and the DJ from the first dance to the last song.

props.title: As much say in the music as you want.
props.lede: Build the list yourself, hand over a do-not-play list and leave the rest, or describe the crowd and let the DJ read it song by song.

props.html: Open format means the DJ plays across genres, so the set is wider than any one list. The songs the live bands play are on the repertoire page, if you want a place to start.

items.q: What does the DJ booking include?
items.a: Decks, a booth and a PA that's the right size for the venue, an announcement microphone for toasts and announcements, setup and pack-down, and the certificate of insurance and W-9 your office needs. It's booked through Signet Artists in Denver, on its own or after a band.

items.q: How much space does the DJ need?
items.a: A booth of about 6 by 4 feet on one dedicated 20-amp circuit, with 45 minutes to set up and 30 to pack down. After a band, the DJ plays through the sound system that's already there.

As loud as the floor wants and the venue allows. During dinner or a toast the DJ plays at a level the tables talk across, and once people are dancing it plays like a party. If your venue has a sound limit or a curfew, give us the number and it's built into the plan.

items.q: How late can the DJ play?
items.a: As late as the venue allows. Added time comes in half-hour blocks, and you can decide it on the night.

items.q: Do you take requests on the night?
items.a: From you, always, and from guests where they fit. A do-not-play list is the part worth spending time on before the event, and a request that would empty the floor gets a straight answer and an alternative.
